steps.stem: An economist said: "Whether the recovery suggested by last quarter's sales figures will be sustained remains highly uncertain, particularly in light of the other developments in the market; what we are seeing is, so far, no more than an early indication." Which of the following sentences expresses the same meaning as the economist's statement?
choices: If we take into account the other developments in the market, it is certain that the recovery suggested by last quarter's sales figures will continue
It is uncertain whether the recovery suggested by last quarter's sales figures accurately reflects the current state of the market
Last quarter's sales figures are admittedly no more than an early indication, but it is already clear that the recovery they suggest will be sustained
Given the other developments in the market, it is doubtful whether the recovery suggested by last quarter's sales figures will last for long
explanation: The economist doubts whether the recovery will last, because of other developments in the market. (1) and (3) turn the doubt into certainty; (2) moves the doubt from the future to the present.

steps.stem: Maya: "At the new restaurant on Elm Street, most diners come back, so I assume the food there is ____." Maya's words are not logical, but they would have been logical had she said ____ instead of "so," ____ instead of ____. Which of the following best completes the text?
choices: disappointing / "therefore" / or "few diners fail to come back" / "most diners come back"
excellent / "even so" / or alternatively "not excellent" / "excellent"
disappointing / "even so" / or "excellent" / "disappointing"
mediocre / "and yet" / and also "quite good" / "mediocre"
explanation: "Most come back, so … disappointing" is illogical; it becomes logical with a concession ("even so") or with a verdict that fits the evidence ("excellent"). (1) swaps in a synonym and a paraphrase, which change nothing; (2) starts from a logical sentence; (4) requires both changes at once, which makes the sentence illogical again.

steps.stem: The following sentence, taken from an announcement about a scholarship, can be understood in two ways: "The scholarship will be awarded only to nursing students who work at the city hospital and residents of the northern district." Which of the following is not possible according to either of the two ways of understanding the sentence?
choices: Yael, who works at the city hospital but is not a nursing student and does not live in the northern district, was awarded the scholarship
Ron, a resident of the northern district who is not a nursing student and does not work at the city hospital, was awarded the scholarship
Shira, a nursing student who lives in the northern district but does not work at the city hospital, was awarded the scholarship
Gil, a resident of the northern district who is not a nursing student and does not work at the city hospital, was not awarded the scholarship
explanation: Reading 1: nursing student + hospital + north; reading 2: (nursing student + hospital) or a resident of the north. Yael is not a nursing student and does not live in the north, so she fails both. Ron and Shira fit reading 2, and "only" never forces an award, so Gil is always possible.

steps.stem: A researcher examined the effect of room temperature on willingness to donate. One group of participants waited for a quarter of an hour in a warm room, and another group in a cool room. Then all the participants were asked to contribute to a fund for renovating a local playground. Those who had waited in the warm room donated considerably more, and the researcher estimated that, since warmth improves mood, these participants had been in a better mood when asked to donate. Which of the following assumptions underlies the researcher's estimate?
choices: A person in a bad mood does not notice the room's temperature, so it makes no difference to them whether the room is warm or cool
A person in a good mood contributes more generously to a cause than a person whose mood is less good
Waiting in a warm room causes people to support playground renovation more than people who waited in a cool room
A good mood causes a person to donate more generously, provided that they have spent time in a warm room beforehand
explanation: The estimate runs warmth → good mood → larger donations; the researcher must assume the second link. (4) adds a condition the estimate does not need; (1) is irrelevant and (3) merely restates the finding.

steps.stem: Noa: "I doubt that I could arrange this violin sonata for the piano, much less for the guitar." Eyal: "What you say implies that you play the piano better than you play the guitar." Eyal's claim is based on the assumption that a musician who finds it easier to arrange a piece ____ plays instrument A better than instrument B.
choices: from instrument A for instrument C than from instrument A for instrument B
from instrument A for instrument C than from instrument B for instrument C
from instrument A for instrument B than from instrument B for instrument A
from instrument C for instrument A than from instrument C for instrument B
explanation: Noa finds violin → piano easier than violin → guitar, and Eyal concludes that she plays the piano better, so ease of arranging for an instrument must reflect command of it: from C (violin) for A (piano) rather than for B (guitar). The other choices put the instruments in the wrong roles.

steps.title: Understanding sentences - the toolkit
steps.intro: What makes a sentence hard, and what to do about it.

head: Difficulty
What to do
rows: Eliminate by structure first; the key expression decides the rest
Find what makes it (il)logical; test each swap
Turn one pair of negatives into a positive at a time
Write both readings ("and" can act as "or"); check each choice against both
Find the unstated link between what was said and the conclusion

tips: "Only" = who can be accepted - not who must be.
The skill runs through all of verbal: no understanding, no conclusions.

steps.stem: A blend is a word formed by joining parts of two existing words so that the new word carries a meaning drawn from both: "brunch," for instance, was formed from "breakfast" and "lunch" and names a meal that takes the place of both. Blends of this kind are of two sorts. In a full blend, each of the two source words contributes a recognizable part: in "brunch," "br-" from "breakfast" and "-unch" from "lunch." In a partial blend, one of the two source words appears whole and only the other is shortened: "motel," for instance, was formed from "motor" and "hotel." Thus "smog," formed from "smoke" and "fog," is a ____ blend, whereas "workaholic," formed from "work" and "alcoholic," is a ____ blend. Which of the following completes the sentence correctly?
choices: full / full
full / partial
partial / full
partial / partial
explanation: In "smog" both sources are cut ("sm-" and "-og"); in "workaholic" the word "work" appears whole and only "alcoholic" is shortened.

steps.stem: Under the same definitions: "Chunnel," formed from "channel" and "tunnel," is a ____ blend, and "guesstimate," formed from "guess" and "estimate," is a ____ blend.
choices: full / full
full / partial
partial / full
partial / partial
explanation: "Chunnel" cuts both sources ("ch-" and "-unnel"); "guesstimate" keeps "guess" whole and shortens only "estimate."

steps.stem: In a lecture on writing for the general public, the historian was asked what makes a good popular history, and answered: "Tell the story as simply as you can — but not more simply than it happened." Which of the following sentences best expresses the historian's intention?
choices: Every good popular history should be simple enough for a reader who knows nothing of the period
A good popular history is built on the simplest and most fundamental of the events it describes
The simplicity of a popular history matters no less than its accuracy
Although simplicity is a virtue in popular history, too much of it distorts the events the book is meant to describe
explanation: The second clause sets a limit on the first: simplify, but not past the truth. (2) turns a rule about telling into a rule about selecting; (3) makes the two equal rather than one bounded by the other; (1) drops the limit altogether.

steps.stem: On the memorial to the poet Yona Amit was engraved a quotation from an interview she gave in 1971: "I was the voice of the valley and its people." The quotation angered many of her admirers, who argued that the sentence from which it was taken showed the poet's characteristic modesty, whereas the quotation on its own made her sound boastful, the reverse of her true character. Which of the following sentences is most likely to be the one from which the quotation was taken?
choices: "I was the voice of the valley and its people, but today, to my sorrow, others lead it"
"Though the price was heavy, as heavy as any burden, I was always the voice of the valley and its people"
"I was the voice of the valley and its people, and of its rivers and its fields"
"If you insist on calling me a spokeswoman, then say that I was the voice of the valley and its people"
explanation: Only (4) makes the claim a concession reluctantly granted — modesty that the excerpt erases. (1) adds regret, (2) sacrifice, (3) scope; none reverses the boast.

steps.stem: Gal invented a new word — "tsuvek." To show his friend what it means, he said: "In the end, tsuvek the people who bought tickets are expected to turn up, so we had better move the show to the small hall." In which of the following sentences does "tsuvek" appear with the same meaning it has in Gal's sentence?
choices: Tsuvek my colleagues objected to the new schedule, so the manager withdrew it the next day
Since tsuvek the shops on the street have closed, the council is considering turning it into a pedestrian mall
The villagers have a reputation for hospitality because tsuvek of them invite passing travelers to eat
Because of the long drought, tsuvek the old olive trees on the hill are still alive, which is why the grove is now protected
explanation: Gal's consequence fixes "tsuvek" as "only a small part of"; only (4) carries a consequence that fits a small remainder. In (1), (2) and (3) the consequences require "most."

steps.stem: It is commonly held that human beings, the apes and dogs are the only animals able to recognize faces. A recent study, however, found that a certain species of wasp also has this ability — a finding that poses a challenge to biologists, since between wasps and human beings there is no direct evolutionary connection, and the wasp's brain is minute. The researchers suggest that the ability developed in wasps independently, because they live in colonies in which recognizing individuals matters. Which of the following claims is NOT implied by the passage?
choices: It is commonly held that the dog's ability to recognize faces is connected with its having lived alongside human beings
It is commonly held that the apes' ability to recognize faces is connected with their evolutionary closeness to human beings
The researchers hold that the ability to recognize faces exists in many animals that have no evolutionary connection with human beings
The researchers hold that the ability to recognize faces may develop in other animals that live in colonies
explanation: The passage reports one such animal, not many; (1), (2) and (4) each follow from what is said about the common view or the researchers' suggestion.

steps.stem: The following sentence can be understood in two different ways: "The struggle of the new department's director with the broadcasting authority continues." Which of the following is NOT one of the two meanings of the sentence?
choices: The struggle that the director is waging against the new department of the broadcasting authority continues
The struggle that the newly appointed director of the department is waging against the broadcasting authority continues
The struggle that the director of the newly established department is waging against the broadcasting authority continues
The struggle that the director of the new department is waging, jointly with the broadcasting authority, against a third party continues
explanation: "New" attaches either to the director or to the department, and "with" reads either as "against" or "alongside" — (2), (3) and (4) are readings the sentence bears; (1) makes the department the opponent, which no reading yields.

steps.stem: Yonatan held a party for his birthday and invited friends and relatives. At the height of the party he rose and announced: "I know every one of you — but a little fewer than half of you I know rather less well than I would like to." How many of the guests does Yonatan know less well than he would like?
choices: Many more than half of them
A little more than half of them
A little fewer than half of them
Many fewer than half of them
explanation: The sentence says it directly; the temptations are to read "I know every one of you" as a claim about knowing well, or to invert the fraction.

steps.stem: A lecturer in medicine wished to illustrate a claim to his students, and said: "If you hear hoofbeats in the street, it is probably horses, not zebras." Which of the following claims is the one the lecturer wished to illustrate?
choices: Before a physician examines the possibility that a patient suffers from a rare disease, he must rule out the possibility that he suffers from a common one
Concentrating on prominent symptoms is liable to lead to a mistaken diagnosis, and a physician must therefore attend to the subtler symptoms
A single symptom may point to more than one disease, and a diagnosis should therefore rest on a combination of symptoms
A physician should not assume that mild symptoms point to a mild disease
explanation: Hoofbeats are the symptom; horses the common cause, zebras the rare one. The other three are sound medical maxims that the image does not express.

steps.stem: Reading difficulties take many forms, among them the following: — misidentifying one of the letters of a word; — exchanging two adjacent letters within a word (usually letters in the middle of the word); — exchanging letters between adjacent words (usually letters in the same position in each word). Which of the following is NOT an example of any of the three difficulties?
choices: Reading the words "calm sea" as "clam sea"
Reading the words "wild boar" as "wild bear"
Reading the words "bright light" as "brigh ligt"
Reading the words "big cat" as "bag cit"
explanation: (1) exchanges adjacent letters within a word; (2) misidentifies a letter; (4) exchanges the vowels between the two words; (3) drops letters, which is none of the three.

steps.stem: The word "pea" is used for the small round green vegetable. Linguists explain, however, that the historical form of the word is "pease": the common form "pea" arose because speakers took "pease," which was itself singular, to be a plural and stripped it of its supposed plural ending. Linguists point out that the same thing happened to the word "cherry," which was formed in the same way from "cherise." Which of the following words could replace "cherry" in the linguists' example?
choices: "berry"
"sherry" (from the older "sherris")
"plum"
"melon"
explanation: Only "sherry" is a singular carved out of a word whose final -s was mistaken for a plural marker, exactly as "pea" and "cherry" were. (1), (3) and (4) were never reshaped in this way.

steps.stem: In a book on politics it was written: "When some matter arises on the public agenda, the American politician asks first of all what the interest of his community is, whereas the European politician asks first of all whether the matter contradicts his ideology. In the end, of course, the American politician also asks whether the matter fits his convictions, and the European also asks what his community wants; the difference between them lies in the order of the questions." Which of the following statements best expresses the central claim of the passage?
choices: American politicians take account of their community's interests, whereas European politicians do not
The public agenda in America is set by the communities, whereas in Europe it is set by ideologies
American and European politicians consider the same two things, but in the opposite order of priority
A politician can serve either his community's interest or his ideology, but not both
explanation: The passage says explicitly that both ask both questions and differ in order; (1) and (2) turn a difference of order into a difference of kind, and (4) invents an incompatibility.

steps.stem: Linguists classify verbs by the number of participants they require. A one-place verb requires only a subject: "The baby slept." A two-place verb requires a subject and an object: "The cat caught the mouse." A three-place verb requires a subject, an object and a recipient: "Dan gave Ruth the key." In which of the following sentences is there a three-place verb?
choices: The river froze during the night
Miriam repaired the fence in the afternoon
The teacher lent Yossi a pencil
Everyone in the room laughed at once
explanation: "Lent" takes a subject, a thing lent and a person lent to; "froze" and "laughed" take only a subject, "repaired" a subject and an object.

steps.stem: In the language of the Aztecs, possessive markers (my, your, his, and so on) are attached to the beginning of a word. Thus "pulo" means "dog," "ipulo" means "his dog," and "mopulo" means "your dog." Likewise, "nokali" means "my house." Therefore, which of the following words is best suited to be the Aztec word for "your house"?
choices: ikali
monokali
kali
mokali
explanation: "Your" is the prefix mo-, seen in "mopulo," and "house" is the stem kali, seen in "nokali." (1) is "his house," (3) is "house," (2) doubles the marker.

steps.stem: Michal passed a note to Shlomi on which she had written: "I am going to tell you at noon what Naama did yesterday." Shlomi returned the note with the words: "But you already told me that later today I would learn what Naama did this week." To clear up the misunderstanding, Michal underlined one word in the sentence she had written and returned the note. Which of the following words is LEAST likely to be the one Michal underlined?
choices: I
at noon
did
yesterday
explanation: Shlomi's version goes wrong on the time of telling ("later today"), the time of the doing ("this week") and perhaps the doing itself; nothing in it concerns who will tell.

steps.stem: Yigal: "I have heard that most of the students pass the examination in the course 'Algebraic Structures,' and so I think that the course is ____." Yigal's words are not logical, but had he said ____ instead of "and so," or ____ instead of ____, they would have been logical. Which of the following completes the passage correctly?
choices: very hard / "and yet" / "easy" / "very hard"
very hard / "and so" / "very hard" / "easy"
easy / "and yet" / "very hard" / "easy"
easy / "and so" / "easy" / "hard"
explanation: A high pass rate followed by "and so… very hard" is illogical; it becomes logical either by turning the connective into a concession ("and yet… very hard") or by turning the verdict to match the evidence ("and so… easy"). (3) starts from a logical sentence; (2) and (4) change nothing.

steps.stem: In grammar, stress is the special emphasis given to one syllable of a word. The fact that in some languages the position of the stress is not fixed — unlike, for instance, Czech, in which the stress always falls on the first syllable — allows pairs of words of different meaning whose only difference is the position of the stress. When such a pair exists in a language, we say that stress in that language is "phonemic." In which of the following sentences does the pair of emphasized words prove that stress in English is phonemic?
choices: The clerk will REcord the complaint and reCORD it again if the first copy is lost
The guard will PRESENT the pass and the visitor will present the PRESENT to the director
She READ the letter yesterday and will READ it again today
The bank by the river is not the bank that holds our money
explanation: "REcord" (noun) and "reCORD" (verb) differ in stress alone. In (2) the two words differ in vowel as well; in (3) the difference is vowel, not stress; in (4) the two words sound the same.

steps.stem: Osnat: "I do not believe anyone could translate the article from German into French, let alone into Spanish." Shlomo: "From your words it follows that you command French better than Spanish." At the basis of Shlomo's claim lies the assumption that whoever finds it easier to translate ____ commands language A better than language B.
choices: from language C into language A than from language C into language B
from language A into language C than from language B into language C
from language A into language B than from language B into language A
from language C into language A than from language A into language C
explanation: Osnat ranks German → French as easier than German → Spanish; Shlomo infers command of the target language — so ease of translating into a language must indicate command of it.

steps.stem: Before you is a sentence from a "positions vacant" notice that can be understood in two ways: "Only architects who hold a first degree in sociology and graduates of a diving course will be accepted for this position." Which of the following is NOT possible under either of the two readings of the sentence?
choices: Elad, a graduate of a diving course who is not an architect and holds no first degree in sociology, was accepted
Nir, a graduate of a diving course who is not an architect and holds no first degree in sociology, was not accepted
Anat, an architect and a graduate of a diving course who holds no first degree in sociology, was accepted
Drora, who holds a first degree in sociology, is not an architect and is not a graduate of a diving course, was accepted
explanation: Under the reading "two groups: sociology-architects, and diving graduates," Drora is in neither; under the reading "one group: architects with both," she is not an architect. (1) and (3) fit the first reading; (2) fits the second.

steps.stem: The prosecutor said to the accused: "Answer yes or no: ____." Counsel for the defense said: "I object to my client's answering this question, for an innocent person cannot answer it without lying." Which of the following questions is NOT suited to complete the prosecutor's words?
choices: Have you stopped smuggling goods through customs?
Could your debts have led you to rob the bank branch?
Did anyone there notice that you were embezzling the funds?
Did you have partners who helped you to evade tax?
explanation: (1), (3) and (4) presuppose the offense, so both "yes" and "no" admit it; (2) asks about a possibility, and an innocent person can answer "no" truthfully.

steps.stem: This spring the migratory birds from East Africa arrived in our region earlier than usual. Nachum argues that it is not reasonable to suppose that the reason is the small amount of rain that fell in East Africa during the winter, since an abundance of offspring causes a late migration. On which of the following assumptions does Nachum's argument rest?
choices: Little rain causes the migratory birds to raise many offspring
In years of drought the birds find it hard to raise many offspring
In rainy years the birds arrive early
In the past winter much rain fell in East Africa
explanation: Nachum's chain is little rain → many offspring → late arrival, which contradicts the early arrival; the first link is the unstated assumption. (2) would make the little-rain explanation work; (3) and (4) are not needed.

steps.stem: A political commentator said: "For the present these are only first signs; and in view of the other phenomena occurring in the country, there is still much doubt whether the mood that found expression in this demonstration will take real hold." Which of the following sentences expresses the same meaning as the commentator's?
choices: It is not clear to what extent the mood expressed in this demonstration will take root, given the other things happening in the country
If we attend to the other phenomena occurring in the country, we cannot doubt that the mood expressed in this demonstration will spread
It is not clear to what extent the mood expressed in this demonstration represents what is happening in the country now
These are indeed only first signs, but for the present there is no doubt that the mood expressed in this demonstration will take hold
explanation: (2) and (4) turn the doubt into certainty; (3) shifts the question from the future to the present.

steps.stem: Woodrow Wilson said: "If I have to give a ten-minute speech on some subject, I need a week to prepare; if fifteen minutes — three days; if I have an hour — I am ready now." Which of the following claims best expresses Wilson's meaning?
choices: The best speeches are the shortest
It is precisely when a person plans less that his speech succeeds more
The length of a speech does not testify to its importance
It is harder to put an idea briefly than to speak about it at length
explanation: Preparation time falls as speaking time grows — brevity is the work. (1), (2) and (3) are not what the joke says.

steps.stem: In one of her articles Dr. Tofi wrote: "I support Dr. Rubin's position, but I am not persuaded by his reasons. In my view, the only reason for allowing prisoners to marry is that preventing it means harming their rights." Which of the following data could be one of Dr. Rubin's reasons?
choices: The law regards all citizens as having equal rights, even though they are members of different sectors of society
After their release from prison, prisoners who married while in prison tend to return to crime less than prisoners who did not
Prisoners who married while in prison used their contact with the outside world to smuggle drugs into the prison
The law recognizes the possibility of denying prisoners' rights, and the right to marry is among them
explanation: Rubin's reasons must support the position and differ from the rights argument; (2) is a practical benefit. (1) is Tofi's own reason; (3) and (4) argue against the position.

steps.stem: A group of researchers examined the effect of consuming caffeine on the ability to concentrate. They gave one group a drink rich in caffeine and the other a drink without caffeine, and then played to both an argument in favor of vegetarianism. The researchers found that those who had consumed caffeine were persuaded by the argument much more, and estimated that, because caffeine raises concentration, these participants had concentrated more on the arguments. Which of the following assumptions underlies the researchers' estimate?
choices: Lack of concentration causes a person not to notice details, and it therefore makes no difference to him whether the drink contains caffeine
Consuming caffeine causes those who need it to support vegetarianism more than those who do not
A person who concentrates on the arguments he hears is persuaded by them more than a person who listens with less attention
Attention to arguments causes a person to be persuaded more, provided that he has consumed caffeine beforehand
explanation: The estimate runs caffeine → concentration → persuasion; the second link is the assumption. (4) adds a condition; (1) and (2) are not needed.

steps.stem: Before you is a sentence from which a part (a word or a few words) is missing: "At the concert were performed, ____ works by composers living in Israel, works by composers born in Israel but living abroad." In which of the following sentences could the missing part be the same as in the sentence above?
choices: Although the director general was expected to announce the reform as early as next week, ____ its implementation will begin only in a few months
____ Dr. Cohen, we succeeded in recruiting for the new study two more researchers from the field of molecular biology
The American government will pursue in the coming years ____ policies of intervention in the affairs of other countries, even if the harm is great
____ participation in the demonstration strengthened the calls to lighten the tax burden on single-parent families
explanation: "Besides" (or "in addition to") fits both. The other sentences need a subject, a verb or an adjective in the gap.

steps.stem: Arik: "My sister told me that yesterday she saw Dafna again, taking part in a flower walk on the Gilboa, and that she enjoyed it very much too." Natali: "____." From Natali's reply it emerges that Arik's sentence can be understood in two ways, and that Natali understood it otherwise than he intended. Which of the following is Natali's reply?
choices: "And where did she see her this time?"
"Your sister went to the Gilboa yesterday, in that stormy weather?"
"And did your sister enjoy it as well?"
"Does your sister also go on walks to see flowers?"
explanation: The participle "taking part" may belong to Dafna or to the sister; Natali gave it to the sister and put her on the mountain. (1), (3) and (4) keep the sister where Arik put her.

steps.stem: The commandment "You shall love your neighbor as yourself" stands at the center of the book "Works of Love" by the philosopher Søren Kierkegaard. The first three chapters of the book are devoted to questions arising from the commandment: the first deals with the question how one can be commanded to love; the second with the question whom we are commanded to love; and the third seeks to answer the question what self-love is. The title of each of the three chapters is the commandment itself, but each time with a different part of it emphasized. Which of the following is NOT suited to be the title of one of the three chapters?
choices: You shall love your NEIGHBOR as yourself
You shall love your neighbor AS YOURSELF
You shall love your neighbor as YOU love yourself
YOU SHALL LOVE your neighbor as yourself
explanation: The emphasized "you" answers none of the three questions; (1) is whom, (2) is self-love, (4) is how love can be commanded.
